## Objective

Implement and verify the roadmap-defined **Scientific configuration authority** for M01. Completion requires every mapped atomic requirement below to exist as working, tested behavior and to satisfy the approved verification target:

> Exact configuration schema/value/hash/fingerprint validation and forbidden-runtime-scientific-decision tests.

No scientific, mathematical, numerical, dataset, chronology, comparator, experiment, statistical, artifact, provenance, reporting, or execution decision may be rediscovered or invented during implementation when it is already fixed by these requirements.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the mapped requirements and their verification evidence:

- Implement every atomic requirement reproduced under **Implementation Requirements**.
- Preserve all formulas, fixed values, gates, identities, chronology rules, failure states, artifact contracts, and claim boundaries those requirements invoke.
- Produce the exact code, configuration/domain contracts, tests, artifacts, evidence, and execution behavior needed for the requirement-specific acceptance checks.
- Integrate only with the upstream/downstream contracts identified in **Dependencies**.
- Keep requirement behavior explicit in production code and tests; no requirement may exist only implicitly in an acceptance criterion, test fixture, implementation note, or undocumented default.

- **REQ-2084** — `§34.2 (L4779)` — The implementation uses deterministic execution wherever supported: enable PyTorch deterministic algorithms.
- **REQ-2085** — `§34.2 (L4780)` — The implementation uses deterministic execution wherever supported: disable cuDNN benchmark/autotuning choices that can change kernels between runs.
- **REQ-2086** — `§34.2 (L4781)` — The implementation uses deterministic execution wherever supported: record Python, NumPy, PyTorch, CUDA/cuDNN, CVXPY, ECOS, LIEF, `pefile`, Android toolchain, UPX, and external baseline/operator tool versions when they are on the producer path.
- **REQ-2087** — `§34.2 (L4782)` — The implementation uses deterministic execution wherever supported: use deterministic dataset ordering before any seeded sampling.
- **REQ-2088** — `§34.2 (L4783)` — The implementation uses deterministic execution wherever supported: use stable canonical serialization/hashing for identities and tie-breaking.
- **REQ-2089** — `§34.2 (L4785)` — A deterministic CPU fallback is part of the relevant environment fingerprint.
- **REQ-2090** — `§34.2 (L4785)` — If a required GPU operation has no deterministic implementation, that producer executes the affected operation on CPU rather than accepting an unspecified numerical tolerance.
- **REQ-2091** — `§34.2 (L4787)` — Numerical tolerance does not authorize scientific threshold changes.
- **REQ-2092** — `§34.2 (L4787)` — Solver results remain subject to the explicit numerical tolerances in §20.
- **REQ-2093** — `§34.3 (L4791)` — Infrastructure faults such as worker interruption, filesystem failure, cluster preemption, or unrelated process crash may be retried with identical scientific inputs and seed identities.
- **REQ-2094** — `§34.3 (L4795)` — Preserve the exact ordered workflow/state flow: `validate existing artifacts → reuse compatible COMPLETE artifacts → identify missing/stale descendants → recompute only the nearest invalid boundary and affected descendants → continue execution`.
- **REQ-2095** — `§34.3 (L4805)` — After a code change, recalculate producer code fingerprints: change outside an artifact's producer/dependency path → artifact remains valid.
- **REQ-2096** — `§34.3 (L4806)` — After a code change, recalculate producer code fingerprints: proven non-semantic change on the path that leaves the producer fingerprint/material dependency digest unchanged → artifact remains valid.
- **REQ-2097** — `§34.3 (L4807)` — After a code change, recalculate producer code fingerprints: material producer/dependency change → artifact and only its descendants become stale.
- **REQ-2098** — `§34.3 (L4808)` — After a code change, recalculate producer code fingerprints: siblings and unrelated branches remain valid.
- **REQ-2099** — `§34.3 (L4810)` — If the regenerated parent has the same dependency fingerprint and deterministic content identity, compatible descendants remain valid.
- **REQ-2100** — `§34.3 (L4810)` — When a parent artifact is regenerated, stale descendants are identified through the reverse dependency index and excluded from active evidence.
- **REQ-2101** — `§34.3 (L4812)` — It may not be rerun with a different seed, altered tolerance, or relaxed scientific constraint merely to obtain a favorable result.
- **REQ-2102** — `§34.3 (L4812)` — Solver divergence, infeasibility, NaN production, conditioning failure, or convergence failure is a numerical/scientific outcome unless independently demonstrated to be infrastructure corruption.
- **REQ-2103** — `§34.3 (L4814)` — Permanently unavailable confirmatory outcomes remain in the evidence record under §17.8.

- **REQ-2106** — `§34.4 (L4823)` — Reproducibility is verified by the ordinary dependency-aware workflow contract: every scientific artifact traces recursively to immutable acquired input checksums, configuration, seeds, producer code, environment, and upstream identities.
- **REQ-2107** — `§34.4 (L4824)` — Reproducibility is verified by the ordinary dependency-aware workflow contract: deterministic producers must regenerate the same content identity from the same complete dependency fingerprint.
- **REQ-2108** — `§34.4 (L4825)` — Reproducibility is verified by the ordinary dependency-aware workflow contract: a clean-room verification, when desired, consists only of removing regenerable `outputs/` and `results/` state and executing the same normal CLI sequence from immutable raw inputs and the authoritative configuration.
- **REQ-2109** — `§34.4 (L4826)` — Reproducibility is verified by the ordinary dependency-aware workflow contract: such verification introduces no new scientific workflow, parameter, threshold, comparator, dataset, or statistical decision.
- **REQ-2110** — `§34.4 (L4828)` — Reproducibility is therefore an invariant of normal execution rather than a separate scientific stage.
- **REQ-2111** — `§34.4 (L4828)` — Scientific decisions may not be changed because confirmatory or later-real outcomes are unfavorable.

Required work:

- Implement every atomic requirement under **Implementation Requirements**, preserving all formulas, fixed values, gates, identities, chronology rules, failure states, artifact contracts, and claim boundaries those requirements invoke; produce the exact code, configuration/domain contracts, tests, artifacts, evidence, and execution behavior needed for the requirement-specific acceptance checks.
- Integrate only with the upstream/downstream contracts identified in **Dependencies**, and keep requirement behavior explicit in production code and tests — no requirement may exist only implicitly in an acceptance criterion, test fixture, implementation note, or undocumented default.

## Objective

Implement and verify the roadmap-defined **Generic workflow registry and CLI/runtime control** for M01. Completion requires every mapped atomic requirement below to exist as working, tested behavior and to satisfy the approved verification target:

> CLI/runtime tests for registry, plan/doctor/run/status, dependency resolution, reuse/resume and prohibited flags.

No scientific, mathematical, numerical, dataset, chronology, comparator, experiment, statistical, artifact, provenance, reporting, or execution decision may be rediscovered or invented during implementation when it is already fixed by these requirements.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the mapped requirements and their verification evidence:

- Implement every atomic requirement reproduced under **Implementation Requirements**.
- Preserve all formulas, fixed values, gates, identities, chronology rules, failure states, artifact contracts, and claim boundaries those requirements invoke.
- Produce the exact code, configuration/domain contracts, tests, artifacts, evidence, and execution behavior needed for the requirement-specific acceptance checks.
- Integrate only with the upstream/downstream contracts identified in **Dependencies**.
- Keep requirement behavior explicit in production code and tests; no requirement may exist only implicitly in an acceptance criterion, test fixture, implementation note, or undocumented default.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-2955** — `§38 (L5653); §42 (L5907)` — The CLI must support the exact command form `fedact run <experiment>`.
- **REQ-2956** — `§38 (L5658)` — Preserve the exact ordered workflow/state flow: `validate existing artifacts → reuse compatible artifacts → identify stale descendants → recompute only what is necessary → continue execution`.
- **REQ-2957** — `§38 (L5668)` — It: resolves the predefined scientific workflow into internal producers and required upstream artifacts.
- **REQ-2958** — `§38 (L5669)` — It: computes the expected dependency fingerprint for each required boundary.
- **REQ-2959** — `§38 (L5670)` — It: validates indexed candidates for `COMPLETE` state, integrity, expected fingerprint, and scientific invariants.
- **REQ-2960** — `§38 (L5671)` — It: reuses every compatible artifact, irrespective of which compatible workflow first produced it.
- **REQ-2961** — `§38 (L5672)` — It: marks incompatible artifacts stale and traverses the reverse dependency index to mark only their descendants stale.
- **REQ-2962** — `§38 (L5673)` — It: cleans incomplete/staging artifacts and removes stale descendants from the active index before regeneration.
- **REQ-2963** — `§38 (L5674)` — It: executes only missing or stale producers from the nearest invalid boundary.
- **REQ-2964** — `§38 (L5675)` — It: executes the requested experiment over its prescribed datasets, cutoffs, cohorts, methods, variants, and seeds.
- **REQ-2965** — `§38 (L5676)` — It: computes only missing/stale metrics and statistical products whose dependencies changed.
- **REQ-2966** — `§38 (L5677)` — It: atomically commits complete artifacts and updates dependency indexes.
- **REQ-2967** — `§38 (L5678)` — It: stores the workflow's scientific outcome.
- **REQ-2968** — `§38 (L5680)` — A valid unfavorable result is a completed scientific workflow.
- **REQ-2969** — `§38 (L5680)` — Infrastructure/runtime failure is an execution failure.
- **REQ-2970** — `§38 (L5680)` — Leakage, incompatible configuration, invalid provenance, or violated scientific invariants make the affected artifact/result invalid rather than silently usable.
- **REQ-2971** — `§38 (L5682)` — A failure in one branch does not automatically mark sibling branches or already-valid parents stale.
- **REQ-2972** — `§39.1 (L5688)` — Internally, compatibility is artifact-specific.
- **REQ-2973** — `§39.1 (L5688)` — The operator-facing run is identified by the selected scientific workflow and its locked execution scope.
- **REQ-2974** — `§39.1 (L5692)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: dataset/raw identity.
- **REQ-2975** — `§39.1 (L5693)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: cutoff and split.
- **REQ-2976** — `§39.1 (L5694)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: client/cohort set.
- **REQ-2977** — `§39.1 (L5695)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: horizon.
- **REQ-2978** — `§39.1 (L5696)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: seed stream used by the artifact producer.
- **REQ-2979** — `§39.1 (L5697)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: material configuration subset.
- **REQ-2980** — `§39.1 (L5698)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: exact upstream artifact identities.
- **REQ-2981** — `§39.1 (L5699)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: representation/checkpoint identity.
- **REQ-2982** — `§39.1 (L5700)` — Each artifact identity is deterministic over the material inputs that determine it, including as applicable: operator/control/calibration/metric definitions.

## Dependencies


### Blocked By

- M01 — I05 Implement Generic Workflow Registry and CLI Runtime Control — provides the validated generic workflow registry and cli/runtime control contract/evidence consumed by this work package.

### Blocks


- M01 — I07 Audit Scientific Configuration, Repository, and Execution Contracts — independently verifies complete requirement coverage, tests, deliverables, provenance, evidence compatibility, and milestone exit readiness after implementation work is complete.
## Implementation Surface

### Production Code

- Roadmap-defined implementation for **Artifact lifecycle, reuse, invalidation and execution state** across `§§38–41, 43.1` and every module/component explicitly named by the mapped requirements.

### Configuration / Domain Contracts

- Typed configuration/domain contracts, enums, dataclasses/Pydantic models, fixed constants, and validation rules explicitly named by the mapped requirements.

### CLI / Application Surface

- Implement/validate only the roadmap-defined execution surfaces named by the mapped requirements: `fedact run <experiment>`, `fedact run <experiment> --overwrite`, `fedact preprocess <dataset> --overwrite`, `fedact smoke --overwrite`, `fedact report <experiment> --overwrite`.

### Tests

- Unit, numerical/scientific, boundary/failure, artifact/provenance, integration, CLI/E2E, smoke, regression, and architecture tests required by the acceptance evidence and the Required Tests section below.

### Artifacts / Reporting

- Persisted evidence and reporting artifacts explicitly required by the mapped requirements; all identity, schema, integrity, completion, dependency, and provenance rules remain authoritative.
- Named paths/artifact identities include: `outputs/`, `outputs/artifacts/`, `outputs/experiments/<descriptive-experiment-name>/`, `outputs/cache/staging/`, `outputs/artifacts/provenance/indexes/artifact_index.jsonl`, `outputs/artifacts/provenance/indexes/dependency_index.json`.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-0488** — `§9.1 (L1532)` — For every rolling external cutoff \(T_j\), a scientific input is permitted only when its source observation and every annotation used by the algorithm were available strictly before the corresponding prospective interval begins.
- **REQ-0489** — `§9.1 (L1536)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence feature fitting or representation training.
- **REQ-0490** — `§9.1 (L1537)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence hyperparameter calibration.
- **REQ-0491** — `§9.1 (L1538)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence client/cohort definition.
- **REQ-0492** — `§9.1 (L1539)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence operator construction or selection.
- **REQ-0493** — `§9.1 (L1540)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence action selection.
- **REQ-0494** — `§9.1 (L1541)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence hardening.
- **REQ-0495** — `§9.1 (L1542)` — Do not allow information first available at or after the cutoff to influence baseline selection or tuning.
- **REQ-0496** — `§9.1 (L1544)` — Later-real observations are evaluation-only.
- **REQ-0497** — `§9.2 > Representation boundary (L1550)` — The encoder associated with cutoff \(T_j\) is trained only from cutoff-safe data and remains immutable throughout nuisance estimation, transition construction, calibration, set construction, action-displacement construction, hardening, and corresponding later-real evaluation.
- **REQ-0498** — `§9.2 > Malicious-history boundary (L1554)` — Only malicious observations and labels available before \(T_j\) may contribute to historical transitions, cohorts, temporal dynamics, and calibration.
- **REQ-0499** — `§9.2 > Control-history boundary (L1558)` — Only benign/control observations and matching attributes available before \(T_j\) may contribute to control construction, nuisance covariance/rank estimation, and uncertainty estimation.
- **REQ-0500** — `§9.2 > Cohort boundary (L1562)` — A later retrospective family annotation may be used only in an explicitly diagnostic analysis and may not define a confirmatory operational cohort.
- **REQ-0501** — `§9.2 > Cohort boundary (L1562)` — Operational cohorts may use only family/context attributes that were available at the historical observation time or by the relevant cutoff.
- **REQ-0502** — `§9.2 > Calibration boundary (L1566)` — Every inner calibration evaluation is fully contained before its external cutoff as specified in §25.
- **REQ-0503** — `§9.2 > Operator-library boundary (L1570)` — An operator executable or validator version used by a cutoff is identified in provenance before evaluating that cutoff.
- **REQ-0504** — `§9.2 > Operator-library boundary (L1570)` — Operator families, parameter grids, construction code, and validity rules are selected without inspection of later-real outcomes.
- **REQ-0505** — `§9.2 > Hardening boundary (L1574)` — The hardened detector for \(T_j\) is completed before the evaluation layer reads observations from \([T_j,T_j+h)\).
- **REQ-0506** — `§9.2 > Evaluation boundary (L1578)` — Later-real data are read only by evaluation producers after all corresponding scientific inputs and decision artifacts have reached `COMPLETE`.

- **REQ-0510** — `§9.3 (L1600)` — An endpoint is eligible for an external cutoff \(T\) only when both windows lie wholly inside

- **REQ-0515** — `§9.3 (L1610)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: [T,T+h).

- **REQ-0562** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1688)` — These values are sanity checks only; the acquisition manifest records the observed values.
- **REQ-0563** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1692)` — Label handling is: use the released `label` field when present and internally consistent.
- **REQ-0564** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1693)` — Label handling is: independently audit it against `vt_count` using benign count `0`, malicious count at least `4`, and discard counts `1,2,3`.
- **REQ-0565** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1694)` — Label handling is: if the released label is absent but `vt_count` is present, derive the binary label by this fixed rule.
- **REQ-0566** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1695)` — Label handling is: if both are present and disagree, exclude the row and record the conflict.
- **REQ-0567** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1697)` — Chronology uses `year_month` unless the acquired raw source provides a more precise timestamp whose semantics are verified and whose availability does not introduce future information.
- **REQ-0568** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1697)` — Malware-family identity uses the released `family` field.
- **REQ-0569** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1697)` — The roadmap does not assume a VirusTotal first-submission timestamp when the acquired release exposes only `year_month`.
- **REQ-0570** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1699)` — The official public features have already undergone the documented variance-threshold selection.
- **REQ-0571** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1701)` — The official public features have already undergone the documented variance-threshold selection. Therefore: when the acquired release is the documented 4,561-feature table, do **not** apply a second variance threshold.
- **REQ-0572** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1702)` — The official public features have already undergone the documented variance-threshold selection. Therefore: when an authorized raw pre-selection feature matrix is acquired instead, fit `VarianceThreshold(threshold=0.001)` using only the corresponding cutoff-safe training population and record the selected feature indices.
- **REQ-0573** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1704)` — In either case, standardization is fitted only on the cutoff-safe training population and then applied unchanged to validation and later observations.
- **REQ-0574** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1706)` — Calendar quarters are temporal windows, not simultaneous clients.
- **REQ-0576** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1706)` — The default real-data execution therefore treats LAMDA as one corpus-level client for action-mechanism evidence.
- **REQ-0577** — `§10.1 > LAMDA (L1706)` — The public LAMDA schema does not establish a natural organization/source client identifier.

- **REQ-0585** — `§10.1 > EMBER2024 (L1716)` — Official documentation describes collection from September 24, 2023 through December 14, 2024 at weekly resolution, with the first 52 weeks used as the original training period and the final 12 weeks as the original test period.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-0655** — `§11.1 (L1818)` — At each representation retraining cutoff, construct the roadmap-defined 64-dimensional cutoff-fixed encoder `E_T`.
- **REQ-0656** — `§11.1 (L1820)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: E_T:x\rightarrow z\in\mathbb R^{64}
- **REQ-0657** — `§11.1 (L1824)` — The cutoff-fixed representation `E_T` is trained only from permitted historical information and remains immutable throughout all scientific producers that reference its checkpoint identity.
- **REQ-0658** — `§11.1 (L1828)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: f_\phi(x)=\sigma(h_\phi(E_T(x))).
- **REQ-0659** — `§11.1 (L1832)` — Hardening changes only the detector head; it never changes the encoder used to define transition/action geometry for that cutoff.
- **REQ-0660** — `§11.2 (L1838)` — Preserve the exact ordered workflow/state flow: `input → Linear(input_dimension, 512) → BatchNorm1d(512) → ReLU → Dropout(0.10) → Linear(512, 256) → BatchNorm1d(256) → ReLU → Dropout(0.10) → Linear(256, 64)`.
- **REQ-0661** — `§11.2 (L1851)` — The 64-dimensional output layer is linear.
- **REQ-0662** — `§11.2 (L1856)` — Support/record the exact roadmap-defined item `Linear(64, 1)`.
- **REQ-0663** — `§11.2 (L1859)` — Sigmoid is applied only for probability-valued inference.
- **REQ-0664** — `§11.2 (L1859)` — Training operates on logits.

- **REQ-0666** — `§11.3 (L1867)` — Randomness is separated as follows: the corresponding `seeds.representation` value initializes encoder parameters.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-0768** — `§12.5 (L2014)` — Every generated candidate passes all four validation layers before statistical evaluation.
- **REQ-0769** — `§12.5 > Structural validity (L2018)` — Under `Structural validity`, the roadmap requires: PE: both `pefile` and LIEF must parse the transformed binary and report the expected machine type.
- **REQ-0770** — `§12.5 > Structural validity (L2019)` — Under `Structural validity`, the roadmap requires: APK: the project APK parser/build tool must parse the package, manifest, resources, and DEX files.
- **REQ-0771** — `§12.5 > Structural validity (L2019)` — Under `Structural validity`, the roadmap requires: package identity must be preserved except for a deterministic temporary signing identity required solely for emulator installation.
- **REQ-0772** — `§12.5 > Execution smoke validity (L2023)` — PE source and transformed samples are executed in the same isolated Windows sandbox image with no external network access for `operators.validation.execution_timeout_seconds`.
- **REQ-0773** — `§12.5 > Execution smoke validity (L2023)` — The sandbox image hash, OS build, launcher, and observation harness are recorded.
- **REQ-0774** — `§12.5 > Execution smoke validity (L2025)` — A transformed sample fails if it introduces a launch/install failure, crash, or ANR not observed for the source under the same harness.
- **REQ-0775** — `§12.5 > Execution smoke validity (L2025)` — APK source and transformed samples are installed and launched in the same project-pinned Android emulator image through ADB.
- **REQ-0776** — `§12.5 > Execution smoke validity (L2025)` — Each receives `operators.validation.android_monkey_events` deterministic UI events generated from the applicable operator seed.
- **REQ-0777** — `§12.5 > Maliciousness preservation (L2029)` — A source that is not detected is `MALICIOUSNESS_VALIDATION_UNAVAILABLE` and is not confirmatory operator evidence.
- **REQ-0778** — `§12.5 > Maliciousness preservation (L2029)` — The source artifact must be detected as malicious by that engine, and the transformed artifact must remain detected.
- **REQ-0779** — `§12.5 > Maliciousness preservation (L2029)` — The study uses ClamAV 1.5.4 with one study-wide signature-database snapshot whose file hashes and publication timestamp are recorded before prospective evaluation.
- **REQ-0780** — `§12.5 > Maliciousness preservation (L2031)` — This independent check supplements, but does not replace, the corpus label.
- **REQ-0781** — `§12.5 > Dynamic-smoke behavior preservation (L2035)` — Remove harness-only events and compute Jaccard similarity between source and transformed event sets.
- **REQ-0782** — `§12.5 > Dynamic-smoke behavior preservation (L2035)` — The sandbox/emulator emits a canonical set of observable events: launched processes/components, created files, modified files, registry or preference writes where available, network-attempt destinations, and loaded modules/libraries.
- **REQ-0783** — `§12.5 > Dynamic-smoke behavior preservation (L2037)` — A generated candidate is behavior-preserving only when its canonical source/transformed event-set Jaccard similarity meets the configured minimum threshold.
- **REQ-0784** — `§12.5 > Dynamic-smoke behavior preservation (L2039)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: J(A,B)=\frac{&#124;A\cap B&#124;}{&#124;A\cup B&#124;} \ge \texttt{operators.validation.minimum＿behavior＿jaccard}.
- **REQ-0785** — `§12.5 > Dynamic-smoke behavior preservation (L2045)` — If both event sets are empty, the check is uninformative and the candidate is not valid for confirmatory operator evidence.
- **REQ-0786** — `§12.6 (L2051)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \text{statistical support}+\text{domain invalid} \Rightarrow \text{REJECT}.
- **REQ-0787** — `§12.6 (L2058)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \frac{ \left\lvert\lbrace\text{operator-eligible source samples with at least one valid nondegenerate candidate}\rbrace\right\rvert }{ \left\lvert\lbrace\text{operator-eligible source samples}\rbrace\right\rvert }.
- **REQ-0788** — `§12.6 (L2066)` — If the denominator is zero or coverage is below `operators.minimum_valid_coverage`, operator-dependent execution emits `ABSTAIN_OPERATOR_COVERAGE_INSUFFICIENT`.
- **REQ-0789** — `§12.7 (L2073)` — Support/record the exact roadmap-defined item `operator_name`.
- **REQ-0790** — `§12.7 (L2074)` — Support/record the exact roadmap-defined item `source_sample_id`.
- **REQ-0791** — `§12.7 (L2075)` — Support/record the exact roadmap-defined item `representation_hash`.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-0100** — `§4.1 (L312)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \Delta M_{k,c,t} = g_{c,t} + U_{k,c,t}a_{k,c,t} + r_{k,c,t} + \ell_{k,c,t} + \varepsilon_{k,c,t}.

- **REQ-0102** — `§4.1 (L328)` — Where: \(U_{k,c,t}a_{k,c,t}\): nuisance lying in the control-estimated nuisance span.
- **REQ-0103** — `§4.1 (L329)` — Where: \(r_{k,c,t}\): nuisance outside the available control span.
- **REQ-0104** — `§4.1 (L330)` — Where: \(\ell_{k,c,t}\): client-private or targeted threat transition.
- **REQ-0105** — `§4.1 (L331)` — Where: \(\varepsilon_{k,c,t}\): sampling and representation noise.
- **REQ-0106** — `§4.1 (L335)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathcal N_{k,c,t}=\mathrm{col}(U_{k,c,t}).
- **REQ-0107** — `§4.1 (L341)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: P_{k,c,t}=I-U_{k,c,t}U_{k,c,t}^{\top},
- **REQ-0108** — `§4.1 (L347)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat P_{k,c,t}=I-\hat U_{k,c,t}\hat U_{k,c,t}^{\top}.
- **REQ-0110** — `§4.1 (L351-L353)` — For every positive-semidefinite matrix \(S\), define the roadmap inverse-seminorm by \(\\|v\\|_{S^{\dagger}}=\sqrt{v^{\top}S^{\dagger}v}\).
- **REQ-0111** — `§4.2 (L359)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \boxed{ \mathcal G_{c,t} = \left\lbrace g: \left\&#124; \hat P_{k,c,t} \left( \Delta M_{k,c,t}-g \right) \right\&#124;_{\hat\Sigma_{k,c,t}^{\dagger}} \le \beta_{k,c,t} \;\forall k, \quad g\in\mathcal R_{c,t} \right\rbrace. }
- **REQ-0112** — `§4.2 (L379)` — \(\mathcal R_{c,t}\) is the pre-cutoff historical plausibility constraint required to bound globally unresolved directions.
- **REQ-0113** — `§4.2 (L381)` — The primary estimand is **not** a reconstructed point \(g\).
- **REQ-0114** — `§4.3 (L387)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: g_{t+1}=Ag_t+w_t, \qquad w_t\in\mathcal W.
- **REQ-0115** — `§4.3 (L395)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \boxed{ \mathcal G^{pred}_{c,T+h} = A^h\mathcal G_{c,T} \oplus \bigoplus_{j=0}^{h-1}A^j\mathcal W. }
- **REQ-0116** — `§4.3 (L404)` — A verified outer convex approximation may substitute for exact propagation only when its coverage behavior is validated before confirmatory experiments.

- **REQ-0118** — `§4.4 (L419)` — If the denominator is below the numerical zero-displacement floor, the action is degenerate and must be rejected.
- **REQ-0119** — `§4.4 (L423)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: (x,o,c,h).
- **REQ-0120** — `§4.5 (L431)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \psi_o(g)=q_o(x)^\top g.
- **REQ-0121** — `§4.5 (L437)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \boxed{ I_o(\mathcal G) = [L_o,U_o] = \left[ \inf_{g\in\mathcal G}q_o^\top g, \sup_{g\in\mathcal G}q_o^\top g \right]. }
- **REQ-0122** — `§4.5 (L450)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: W_o=U_o-L_o.
- **REQ-0123** — `§4.6 > Positively identified (L458)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: L_o\ge\tau_{align}.
- **REQ-0124** — `§4.6 > Negatively identified (L464)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: U_o\lt \tau_{align}.

## Objective

Implement and verify the roadmap-defined **Assumptions, finite-sample uncertainty and theoretical guarantees** for M04. Completion requires every mapped atomic requirement below to exist as working, tested behavior and to satisfy the approved verification target:

> Bootstrap/subspace/coverage/conditioning/non-identification fixtures and proof obligations match executable estimators.

No scientific, mathematical, numerical, dataset, chronology, comparator, experiment, statistical, artifact, provenance, reporting, or execution decision may be rediscovered or invented during implementation when it is already fixed by these requirements.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the mapped requirements and their verification evidence:

- Implement every atomic requirement reproduced under **Implementation Requirements**.
- Preserve all formulas, fixed values, gates, identities, chronology rules, failure states, artifact contracts, and claim boundaries those requirements invoke.
- Produce the exact code, configuration/domain contracts, tests, artifacts, evidence, and execution behavior needed for the requirement-specific acceptance checks.
- Integrate only with the upstream/downstream contracts identified in **Dependencies**.
- Keep requirement behavior explicit in production code and tests; no requirement may exist only implicitly in an acceptance criterion, test fixture, implementation note, or undocumented default.

- **REQ-0316** — `§8.1 > Valid operator library (L922)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathcal O_T(x).

- **REQ-0318** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L934)` — Let \(\Delta=\texttt{temporal.transition＿interval＿months}\).
- **REQ-0319** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L936); §9.3 (L1594)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: W_t^-=[t-2\Delta,t-\Delta), \qquad W_t^+=[t-\Delta,t).
- **REQ-0320** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L944)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat\mu^{M,-}_{k,c,t} = \frac1{n^{M,-}_{k,c,t}} \sum_{i\in M(k,c,W_t^-)}E_T(x_i),
- **REQ-0321** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L950)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat\mu^{M,+}_{k,c,t} = \frac1{n^{M,+}_{k,c,t}} \sum_{i\in M(k,c,W_t^+)}E_T(x_i),
- **REQ-0322** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L958)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: y_{k,c,t} = \hat\mu^{M,+}_{k,c,t} - \hat\mu^{M,-}_{k,c,t}.
- **REQ-0323** — `§8.2 > Cutoff-safe malicious transition (L964)` — Both malicious sides must independently satisfy `identification.minimum_support_per_class`.
- **REQ-0324** — `§8.2 > Matched control-transition replicates (L970)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: b^{(s)}_{k,c,t} = \hat\mu^{B,s,+}_{k,c,t} - \hat\mu^{B,s,-}_{k,c,t}.
- **REQ-0325** — `§8.2 > Matched control-transition replicates (L978)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: m_s = \left(\frac1{n_s^-}+\frac1{n_s^+}\right)^{-1}, \qquad \omega_s=\frac{m_s}{\sum_jm_j}.
- **REQ-0326** — `§8.2 > Matched control-transition replicates (L985)` — At least `identification.minimum_control_transition_replicates` finite control-transition replicates are required after dataset-specific matching.
- **REQ-0327** — `§8.2 > Matched control-transition replicates (L985)` — Otherwise the client is unusable for identification and emits `ABSTAIN_NO_USABLE_CONTROL`.
- **REQ-0328** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L991)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \bar b=\sum_s\omega_sb^{(s)}
- **REQ-0329** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L997)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat C^B_{\mathrm{raw}} = \sum_s\omega_s (b^{(s)}-\bar b)(b^{(s)}-\bar b)^\top.
- **REQ-0330** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1005)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge\lambda_d\ge0.
- **REQ-0331** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1009)` — The admissible candidate ranks are the configured candidates not exceeding
- **REQ-0332** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1011)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: r_{\max}^{\mathrm{data}} = \min\lbrace d-1,\; S-1,\; \texttt{identification.nuisance＿rank.maximum} \rbrace,
- **REQ-0333** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1020)` — `S` in the data-driven maximum-rank rule is the number of control-transition replicates.
- **REQ-0334** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1022)` — Compute the executable eigengap ratio `Gamma_r` for every admissible nuisance rank `r`.
- **REQ-0335** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1024)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \Gamma_r = \frac{\lambda_r} {\max\lbrace \lambda_{r+1}, \texttt{numerical.rank＿clip＿epsilon＿relative}\lambda_1, \texttt{numerical.scale＿standardization＿floor} \rbrace}.
- **REQ-0336** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1034)` — If none qualifies, the client emits `ABSTAIN_WEAK_EIGENGAP`.
- **REQ-0337** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1034)` — The selected rank is the largest admissible \(r\) whose ratio meets the calibrated eigengap requirement.
- **REQ-0338** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1036)` — Otherwise the client emits `ABSTAIN_UNSTABLE_NUISANCE_RANK`.
- **REQ-0339** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1036)` — Rank stability is evaluated by a weighted nonparametric bootstrap of the \(S\) control-transition replicates using `identification.nuisance_rank.bootstrap_resamples` resamples and the `seeds.calibration` stream.
- **REQ-0340** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1036)` — The selected rank must equal the full-sample selected rank in at least `identification.nuisance_rank.minimum_bootstrap_stability_fraction` of resamples.
- **REQ-0341** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1040)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat C^B = \hat C^B_{\mathrm{raw}}+\eta I,
- **REQ-0342** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1045)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \eta = \max\left\lbrace \texttt{numerical.scale＿standardization＿floor}, \; c\frac{\mathrm{tr}(\hat C^B_{\mathrm{raw}})}d \right\rbrace,
- **REQ-0343** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1054)` — The covariance-regularization coefficient `c` is selected from `identification.covariance_regularization`.
- **REQ-0344** — `§8.2 > Nuisance covariance and rank (L1058)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat P_k=I-\hat U_k\hat U_k^\top.
- **REQ-0345** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1064)` — Define the covariance of the mean displacement
- **REQ-0346** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1064)` — Let \(\hat S^{M,-}\) and \(\hat S^{M,+}\) be unbiased sample covariance matrices of the cutoff-fixed embeddings in \(W_t^-\) and \(W_t^+\).
- **REQ-0347** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1066)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat V^M = \frac{\hat S^{M,-}}{n^{M,-}} + \frac{\hat S^{M,+}}{n^{M,+}},
- **REQ-0348** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1073)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{raw}} = \hat P_k\hat V^M\hat P_k,
- **REQ-0349** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1080)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \hat\Sigma_k = \hat\Sigma_{\mathrm{raw}}+\zeta I,
- **REQ-0350** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1085)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \zeta = \max\left\lbrace \texttt{numerical.scale＿standardization＿floor}, \; c\frac{\mathrm{tr}(\hat V^M)}d \right\rbrace.
- **REQ-0351** — `§8.2 > Malicious-transition covariance (L1094)` — Every inverse norm in FedACT uses the positive-definite \(\hat\Sigma_k^{-1}\); a pseudoinverse is used only in explicitly named point-estimator diagnostics.

## Objective

Implement and verify the roadmap-defined **Synthetic generator, geometry and smoke validation** for M05. Completion requires every mapped atomic requirement below to exist as working, tested behavior and to satisfy the approved verification target:

> Generator invariants, deterministic replay and smoke manifest.

No scientific, mathematical, numerical, dataset, chronology, comparator, experiment, statistical, artifact, provenance, reporting, or execution decision may be rediscovered or invented during implementation when it is already fixed by these requirements.

## Scope

Implement only the work required to satisfy the mapped requirements and their verification evidence:

- Implement every atomic requirement reproduced under **Implementation Requirements**.
- Preserve all formulas, fixed values, gates, identities, chronology rules, failure states, artifact contracts, and claim boundaries those requirements invoke.
- Produce the exact code, configuration/domain contracts, tests, artifacts, evidence, and execution behavior needed for the requirement-specific acceptance checks.
- Integrate only with the upstream/downstream contracts identified in **Dependencies**.
- Keep requirement behavior explicit in production code and tests; no requirement may exist only implicitly in an acceptance criterion, test fixture, implementation note, or undocumented default.

- **REQ-0838** — `§14 (L2185)` — A comparator that depends on an external published implementation is acquired from the named official author repository when available; the exact commit/release and dependency environment are recorded before that comparator is used.
- **REQ-0839** — `§14 (L2185)` — Every comparator below has an executable identity.
- **REQ-0840** — `§14 (L2185)` — If the publication and public implementation together do not specify enough information to reproduce the method without inventing scientific hyperparameters, that comparator is `NOT_APPLICABLE` under the explicit eligibility rule below rather than being approximated ad hoc.
- **REQ-0841** — `§14.1 (L2189)` — All point estimators use the same cutoff-safe transition/control summaries as FedACT unless the baseline definition intentionally removes controls.
- **REQ-0842** — `§14.1 (L2191)` — Define the stacked whitened projected system `A`, `b`, and `H` exactly as in §14.1.
- **REQ-0843** — `§14.1 (L2193)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: A= \begin{bmatrix} \hat\Sigma_1^{-1/2}\hat P_1\\ \vdots\\ \hat\Sigma_K^{-1/2}\hat P_K \end{bmatrix}, \qquad b= \begin{bmatrix} \hat\Sigma_1^{-1/2}\hat P_1y_1\\ \vdots\\ \hat\Sigma_K^{-1/2}\hat P_Ky_K \end{bmatrix}, \qquad H=A^\top A.
- **REQ-0845** — `§14.1 (L2213)` — Implement comparator `Raw malicious-transition forecast` exactly as: effective-support-weighted mean of \(y_k\), followed by the same scalar temporal model as FedACT.
- **REQ-0847** — `§14.1 (L2214)` — Implement comparator `Matched benign subtraction` exactly as: subtract each client's weighted mean control transition \(\bar b_k\) from \(y_k\), then combine client vectors by geometric median.
- **REQ-0849** — `§14.1 (L2215)` — Implement comparator `Projected-inverse point reconstruction` exactly as: \(A^\dagger b\).
- **REQ-0851** — `§14.1 (L2216)` — Implement comparator `Best individual client` exactly as: minimum-norm solution from the client having smallest \(\beta_k\); ties by larger malicious effective support then lexical client id.
- **REQ-0853** — `§14.1 (L2217)` — Implement comparator `Single pooled nuisance subspace` exactly as: estimate one nuisance basis from all eligible control-transition replicates pooled with effective-support weights, then solve the corresponding point system.
- **REQ-0855** — `§14.1 (L2218)` — Implement comparator `Average projected residual` exactly as: effective-support-weighted mean of \(\hat P_ky_k\).
- **REQ-0857** — `§14.1 (L2219)` — Implement comparator `Standard pseudoinverse` exactly as: \(A^\dagger b\) with numerical pseudoinverse cutoff `numerical.rank_clip_epsilon_relative`.
- **REQ-0859** — `§14.1 (L2220)` — Implement comparator `Regularized point reconstruction` exactly as: \((H+\lambda I)^{-1}A^\top b\), with \(\lambda=\max(\epsilon_{\rm scale},c_{\rm ridge}\mathrm{tr}(H)/d)\).
- **REQ-0861** — `§14.1 (L2221)` — Implement comparator `Covariance-weighted projected point` exactly as: weighted least-squares solution of the stacked system above.
- **REQ-0863** — `§14.1 (L2222)` — Implement comparator `Robust raw aggregation` exactly as: geometric median of \(y_k\).
- **REQ-0865** — `§14.1 (L2223)` — Implement comparator `Nuisance projection without global intersection` exactly as: geometric median of \(\hat P_ky_k\).
- **REQ-0867** — `§14.1 (L2224)` — Implement comparator `Same feasible set, generic robust training, no certificate` exactly as: rank valid actions by alignment to the propagated Chebyshev center and use the same action count/hardening budget without the interval certificate.
- **REQ-0869** — `§14.1 (L2225)` — Implement comparator `Point estimate plus matched isotropic uncertainty` exactly as: center the propagated point estimate in an L2 ball whose radius is selected by the same nested inner-cutoff procedure to match FedACT's certification rate as closely as possible.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-0965** — `§16.1 > Set coverage (L2353)` — Compute set coverage on known-truth synthetic data using the roadmap indicator-average definition.
- **REQ-0966** — `§16.1 > Set coverage (L2355)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{Coverage}_{set} = \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N \mathbf1[g_i^{true}\in\mathcal G_i].
- **REQ-0967** — `§16.1 > Action-interval coverage (L2363)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{Coverage}_{action} = \frac1N\sum_i \mathbf1[q_i^\top g_i^{true}\in[L_i,U_i]].
- **REQ-0968** — `§16.1 > Action width (L2371)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: W_o=U_o-L_o.
- **REQ-0969** — `§16.1 > Certification rate (L2377)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{CertRate} = \frac{\left\lvert\lbrace\text{valid candidate actions certified}\rbrace\right\rvert} {\left\lvert\lbrace\text{valid candidate actions evaluated}\rbrace\right\rvert}.
- **REQ-0970** — `§16.1 > Ambiguity rate (L2385)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{AmbRate} = \frac{\left\lvert\lbrace L_o\lt \tau_{align}\le U_o\rbrace\right\rvert} {\left\lvert\lbrace\text{valid candidate actions evaluated}\rbrace\right\rvert}.
- **REQ-0971** — `§16.1 > Abstention rate (L2393)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{AbstentionRate} = \frac{\left\lvert\lbrace\text{eligible cohort/horizon units with no actionable certificate}\rbrace\right\rvert} {\left\lvert\lbrace\text{eligible cohort/horizon units}\rbrace\right\rvert}.
- **REQ-0972** — `§16.1 > False-certification rate (L2401)` — Compute false-certification rate on known-truth simulation using the roadmap definition and undefined case.
- **REQ-0973** — `§16.1 > False-certification rate (L2403)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: R_o^{true}=\mathbf1[q_o^\top g^{true}\ge\tau_{align}],
- **REQ-0974** — `§16.1 > False-certification rate (L2407)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \mathrm{FCR} = \frac{ \sum_o\mathbf1[\mathrm{Cert}_o=1\land R_o^{true}=0] }{ \sum_o\mathbf1[\mathrm{Cert}_o=1] }.
- **REQ-0975** — `§16.1 > False-certification rate (L2416)` — If no action is certified, report `UNDEFINED_NO_CERTIFICATES`.
- **REQ-0976** — `§16.2 (L2420)` — For real data, §Configuration-linked definitions constructs \(\hat g^{real}_{c,(T,T+h]}\).
- **REQ-0977** — `§16.2 (L2422)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: A_o^{real}=q_o^\top\hat g^{real}_{c,(T,T+h]}.
- **REQ-0978** — `§16.2 (L2428)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: R_o^{real} = \mathbf1[ A_o^{real}\ge\tau_{align} ].
- **REQ-0979** — `§16.2 (L2435)` — The threshold is the same pre-cutoff \(\tau_{align}\) used by the corresponding certificate; no later-real relevance threshold is tuned separately.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-1651** — `§25 (L3893)` — Nested calibration is generated automatically the first time a downstream real-data workflow requires calibrated values for a dataset/external cutoff.

- **REQ-1655** — `§25 (L3903)` — Use every eligible inner cutoff at `temporal.cutoff_step_months`.
- **REQ-1656** — `§25.1 (L3909)` — Nested calibration may vary eigengap requirement from `identification.eigengap_ratio.candidates` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.

- **REQ-1658** — `§25.1 (L3911)` — Nested calibration may vary control-span alpha from `identification.control_span_violation.sensitivity_alpha` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.
- **REQ-1659** — `§25.1 (L3912)` — Nested calibration may vary private-transition alpha from `identification.private_contamination.sensitivity_alpha` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.
- **REQ-1660** — `§25.1 (L3913)` — Nested calibration may vary historical-plausibility radius multiplier from `identification.historical_plausibility_radius.sensitivity_multipliers` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.
- **REQ-1661** — `§25.1 (L3914)` — Nested calibration may vary alignment percentile from `certification.alignment_threshold.percentile_candidates` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.
- **REQ-1662** — `§25.1 (L3915)` — Nested calibration may vary ambiguity-width percentile from `certification.ambiguity_width.percentile_candidates` as one of the only permitted calibration dimensions.
- **REQ-1663** — `§25.1 (L3917)` — Nuisance rank is **derived** inside each candidate by the §8.2 eigengap rule; it is not independently grid-searched.

- **REQ-1673** — `§25.1 (L3930)` — Keep leave-one-client-out stability fraction fixed during nested calibration; do not tune it.
- **REQ-1674** — `§25.1 (L3931)` — Keep primary hardening action cap fixed during nested calibration; do not tune it.
- **REQ-1675** — `§25.1 (L3932)` — Keep numerical solver tolerances fixed during nested calibration; do not tune it.
- **REQ-1676** — `§25.1 (L3934)` — Its configured alternative values are sensitivity-only.
- **REQ-1677** — `§25.1 (L3934)` — The covariance-regularization primary value is used in confirmatory calibration.
- **REQ-1678** — `§25.2 (L3940)` — For each inner cutoff: the alignment threshold is the selected percentile of the pooled **inner-historical** point-alignment distribution computed from the propagated Chebyshev-center point and valid action directions.
- **REQ-1679** — `§25.2 (L3941)` — For each inner cutoff: the ambiguity threshold is the selected percentile of the pooled **inner-historical** FedACT action-width distribution.
- **REQ-1680** — `§25.2 (L3942)` — For each inner cutoff: the forecast-diameter threshold is the fixed configured percentile of historical \(D_{\mathrm{box}}\) values.
- **REQ-1681** — `§25.2 (L3943)` — For each inner cutoff: all percentiles use the §17 linear quantile rule.
- **REQ-1682** — `§25.2 (L3945)` — No inner later-real outcome is used to construct a percentile threshold; inner later-real observations are used only to evaluate the candidate.
- **REQ-1683** — `§25.3 (L3951)` — Nested-calibration candidate validity requires all required client/control/set quality gates are satisfied for enough units to retain at least the minimum paired cutoff count.

- **REQ-1690** — `§25.3 (L3960)` — Synthetic known-truth coverage remains the direct estimator-validation evidence.
- **REQ-1691** — `§25.4 (L3966)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: highest mean inner-cutoff certificate precision.
- **REQ-1692** — `§25.4 (L3967)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: highest mean inner-cutoff certification rate.
- **REQ-1693** — `§25.4 (L3968)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: smallest median inner-cutoff action width.
- **REQ-1694** — `§25.4 (L3969)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: larger realized minimum eligible support.
- **REQ-1695** — `§25.4 (L3970)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: smaller ambiguity-width percentile.
- **REQ-1696** — `§25.4 (L3971)` — Among valid candidates, select lexicographically by the following objective hierarchy: lexicographically smallest canonical candidate-configuration hash.
- **REQ-1697** — `§25.4 (L3973)` — All means first aggregate planned random seeds within cutoff according to §17.3 and then average inner cutoffs equally.
- **REQ-1698** — `§25.4 (L3975)` — This ordering operationalizes the scientific priorities: validity is a hard gate, false certification is controlled before utility is optimized, and useful selective certification is favored only among valid configurations.
- **REQ-1699** — `§25.5 (L3979)` — Hardening weight is selected after the identification/certification candidate above is fixed.
- **REQ-1700** — `§25.5 (L3981)` — A weight is admissible only when its mean clean FNR degradation is at or below `hardening.weight.maximum_clean_fnr_degradation_percentage_points`.
- **REQ-1701** — `§25.5 (L3981)` — For each configured hardening weight, train/evaluate only on the nested inner histories/pseudo-futures using §8.3.
- **REQ-1702** — `§25.5 (L3983)` — Among admissible weights, select the weight with the largest mean inner-cutoff absolute early-FNR reduction.
- **REQ-1703** — `§25.5 (L3983)` — If no weight is admissible, hardening for that external cutoff returns `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`; identification/certification may still execute without claiming hardening benefit.
- **REQ-1704** — `§25.5 (L3983)` — Ties within `numerical.projection_tie_tolerance` go to the smaller weight.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-1720** — `§26 > Scientific question (L4011)` — Does the FedACT action certificate contain later-real information beyond a point estimate, action validity alone, and random valid augmentation?
- **REQ-1721** — `§26.1 (L4017)` — At each external cutoff/cohort/horizon: **Certified actions** — FedACT-certified under §8.3.
- **REQ-1722** — `§26.1 (L4018)` — At each external cutoff/cohort/horizon: **Point-positive ambiguous actions** — FedACT-ambiguous actions whose propagated Chebyshev-center score satisfies.
- **REQ-1723** — `§26.1 (L4019); §28 > Point-versus-Set Ablation (L4189)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: q_o^\top\hat g^{pred}_{center}\ge\tau_{align};
- **REQ-1724** — `§26.1 (L4022)` — \]: **Negatively identified actions** — \(U_o\lt \tau_{align}\).
- **REQ-1725** — `§26.1 (L4023)` — \]: **Matched random valid actions** — sampled from domain-valid nondegenerate candidates without using FedACT interval/point scores.
- **REQ-1726** — `§26.1 (L4025)` — The propagated point used in group 2 is uniquely the Chebyshev-center point implied by §8.3; no alternative point estimator may be selected post hoc.
- **REQ-1727** — `§26.2 (L4031)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: R_o^{real} = \mathbf1[ q_o^\top\hat g^{real}_{c,(T,T+h]} \ge\tau_{align} ].
- **REQ-1728** — `§26.2 (L4039)` — The same pre-cutoff threshold \(\tau_{align}\) defines certificate semantics and later-real relevance.
- **REQ-1729** — `§26.3 (L4043)` — Let \(N_{cert}\) be the number of certified actions in one cutoff/cohort/horizon.
- **REQ-1730** — `§26.3 > Point comparator at matched certification count (L4047)` — Compare their later-real precision with the precision of the \(N_{cert}\) FedACT certificates.
- **REQ-1731** — `§26.3 > Point comparator at matched certification count (L4047)` — To compare precision at a matched certification rate, rank every valid candidate by propagated Chebyshev-center point score descending, with canonical action identity as deterministic tie-breaker, and label the top \(N_{cert}\) point actions as point-selected.
- **REQ-1732** — `§26.3 > Point comparator at matched certification count (L4049)` — If \(N_{cert}=0\), matched precision is undefined and the cutoff contributes to certification/abstention metrics but not precision inference.
- **REQ-1733** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4053)` — Sample \(N_{cert}\) candidates without replacement using the applicable `seeds.operator` index.
- **REQ-1734** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4055)` — Sample \(N_{cert}\) candidates without replacement using the applicable `seeds.operator` index. Match in this priority order: same cutoff, cohort, horizon, source sample, and atomic/composed action count.
- **REQ-1735** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4056)` — Sample \(N_{cert}\) candidates without replacement using the applicable `seeds.operator` index. Match in this priority order: if no unused candidate satisfies all fields, same cutoff, cohort, horizon, and source sample.
- **REQ-1736** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4057)` — Sample \(N_{cert}\) candidates without replacement using the applicable `seeds.operator` index. Match in this priority order: if still unavailable, same cutoff, cohort, horizon.
- **REQ-1737** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4059)` — Never relax domain validity or horizon.
- **REQ-1738** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4059)` — Record the matching level for every selected action.
- **REQ-1739** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4061)` — At least `certification.random_matching.minimum_exact_or_source_fraction` of random matches must satisfy levels 1–2; otherwise that cutoff's certified-vs-random contrast is `INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`.
- **REQ-1740** — `§26.3 > Matched random valid actions (L4063)` — Execute random matching for every planned operator seed and average the resulting cutoff-level random endpoint before confirmatory inference according to §17.3.
- **REQ-1741** — `§26.4 (L4069)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: source training population.
- **REQ-1742** — `§26.4 (L4070)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: number of challenges.
- **REQ-1743** — `§26.4 (L4071)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: per-sample action cap.
- **REQ-1744** — `§26.4 (L4072)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: detector initialization.
- **REQ-1745** — `§26.4 (L4073)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: optimization budget.
- **REQ-1746** — `§26.4 (L4074)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: clean-cost constraint.
- **REQ-1747** — `§26.4 (L4075)` — When an action group is used for hardening, match: evaluation horizon.
- **REQ-1748** — `§26.5 (L4081)` — Primary: later-real action alignment.
- **REQ-1749** — `§26.5 (L4082)` — Primary: certificate precision at the matched certification count.
- **REQ-1750** — `§26.5 (L4086)` — Secondary: Spearman rank alignment between \(L_o\) and later-real alignment.
- **REQ-1751** — `§26.5 (L4087)` — Secondary: action width.
- **REQ-1752** — `§26.5 (L4088)` — Secondary: defensive effect when used.
- **REQ-1753** — `§26.6 (L4094)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \text{Certified} \gt \text{Point-positive ambiguous} \gt \text{Matched random valid}
- **REQ-1754** — `§26.6 (L4100)` — Evaluate the required certified > point-positive ambiguous > matched-random pattern for prospective relevance using the exact inferential and decision rules in §17.

## Implementation Requirements

- **REQ-1835** — `§29 (L4260)` — LAMDA's default one-client execution is therefore not included unless an acquired release passes §10.2 with a genuine multi-client field.
- **REQ-1836** — `§29 (L4260)` — This workflow executes only where at least two quality-eligible clients exist for the relevant condition.
- **REQ-1837** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4264)` — Compare each local result with the multi-client intersection on the shared action population.
- **REQ-1838** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4264)` — For every eligible client, construct the complete local FedACT set using only that client and the same historical plausibility rule.
- **REQ-1839** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4266)` — Aggregate local performance by taking the median local action width/relevance endpoint within cutoff before comparison with the federated endpoint.
- **REQ-1840** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4270)` — Measure action width.
- **REQ-1841** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4271)` — Measure ambiguity/certification.
- **REQ-1842** — `§29 > Local versus Federated Identification (L4272)` — Measure certification precision.
- **REQ-1843** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4276)` — Synthetic execution uses §21 with identical total malicious/control support under `redundant` and `complementary` geometry.
- **REQ-1844** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4278)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates.
- **REQ-1845** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4280)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: choose a source with at least twice the support required to create two disjoint pseudo-clients in every required malicious/control cell.
- **REQ-1846** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4281)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: deterministically split that source by hash order into two disjoint equal-support pseudo-clients.
- **REQ-1847** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4282)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: cap each pseudo-client cell so the combined malicious/control count equals the corresponding combined count used by the observed Win32/Win64 condition.
- **REQ-1848** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4283)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: execute the same complete client-estimation and FedACT intersection procedure.
- **REQ-1849** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4284)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: when both Win32 and Win64 can supply a redundant pair, compute both source-specific redundant results and average them within cutoff.
- **REQ-1850** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4285)` — For the real two-source EMBER2024 substrate, the **complementary** condition is the observed Win32/Win64 pair when both pass all gates. The matched **redundant** diagnostic comparator is constructed separately for each source: if neither source has enough support for the matched construction, the real redundant contrast is `NOT_APPLICABLE_INSUFFICIENT_MATCHED_SUPPORT`.
- **REQ-1851** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4287)` — The pseudo-client condition is explicitly a diagnostic matched-redundancy comparator and does not create a natural-client claim.
- **REQ-1852** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4291)` — Use/verify the roadmap-defined mathematical relation exactly: \Delta W_o = W_o^{redundant} - W_o^{complementary}.
- **REQ-1853** — `§29 > Redundant versus Complementary Federation (L4297)` — Positive values favor complementary identification.
